summary: This photoredox cross-coupling reaction utilizes single electron transfer (SET) mechanism with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photocatalyst (2 mol%) and tBu-TMG base in DMF solvent under 440 nm blue LED irradiation. The optimized flow process operates at 50°C with a 12-minute residence time at 0.83 mL/min flow rate in a segmented flow reactor using FEP tubing with 10 mL reactor volume. Flow conditions achieved 88% yield compared to 81% yield under batch conditions at 30°C, representing an 8.6% improvement in yield. The primary advantage of flow was enabling higher operating temperature (50°C vs 30°C) with superior heat transfer control, while providing predictable scale-up capability to hundreds of mg/h production rates with significantly shorter reaction times.

summary: This Csp2-Csp3 cross-coupling reaction employs photoredox/nickel dual catalysis using Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 as the photocatalyst at 2.5 mol% loading with 2,6-lutidine base in THF solvent. The reaction operates at 30°C with blue LED irradiation at 450 nm in a Vapourtec E-series UV-150 flow reactor (10 mL volume) with a 40-minute residence time at 0.25 mL/min flow rate. Flow processing achieved a remarkable 36-fold intensification, reducing reaction time from 24 hours in batch to just 40 minutes while simultaneously improving yield from 60% to 71%. The dramatic improvement stems from the superior light penetration and photon efficiency of the blue LED system compared to the CFL light source used in batch, combined with the optimized irradiation geometry in the dedicated flow photoreactor.

summary: This C-N cross-coupling reaction employs photoredox/nickel dual catalysis using Ru(bpy)3(PF6)2 as the photocatalyst with DABCO base in DMSO solvent. The flow process operates at 80°C with a 60-minute residence time (0.167 mL/min flow rate) in a UV-150 photochemical reactor (10 mL volume) under 450 nm LED irradiation. Compared to batch conditions (55°C, 240 minutes, 42% yield), the flow system achieved 78% yield with a 4-fold reduction in reaction time. The flow advantage stems from improved heat transfer enabling higher temperature operation (80°C vs 55°C), continuous processing, and better temperature control, resulting in an 85.7% improvement in yield efficiency.
